_comment: What is out there, and what it implies we should build. Refreshed by a human (or the Horizon agent) with web access; read by tools/productctl benchmark, which has none. See docs/product-benchmark.md.

sources.claim: Connections has overtaken Wordle as the most-played NYT puzzle by daily active players.
Connections' design uses deliberate misdirection, four allowed mistakes, and 'one away' near-miss feedback.
Puzzmo is laid out like a magazine page; progress on each puzzle is memorialised on the hub, and puzzles show a visual preview before you start.
Puzzmo's lineup is modernised classics (Cross|word, Really Bad Chess) alongside originals, with groups and leaderboards for low-stakes competition.
Daily puzzles are the dominant new category; the most-played browser games are daily puzzles, durable .io multiplayer, and classics that refuse to fade.
2026 UI: motion earns its keep by guiding rather than flashing; micro-interactions drive engagement; mobile visuals are coupled to haptic feedback.
Our own Sudoku proves a daily puzzle can be generated rather than curated: seeded from the date, verified to have exactly one solution, zero content cost.

candidates.name: A magazine-style daily hub where every game's result is memorialised
candidates.evidence: Puzzmo's core structure: a page of puzzle widgets, progress shown when you navigate back

candidates.name: Show the daily streak on the hub
candidates.evidence: The daily already keeps a streak and shows it on /daily; the hub built in #62 does not surface it, which is where Puzzmo puts it
candidates.constraint: Snake deliberately has no streak — game-room.js states the site is not built on loss aversion. This is the daily only.

candidates.name: Near-miss feedback: tell them how close they were
candidates.evidence: Connections' 'one away' is repeatedly named as the reason a loss still feels like information

candidates.name: Play any previous day's puzzle
candidates.evidence: The seeded generator already makes every past day reproducible at zero storage cost

candidates.name: Haptic feedback on mobile via navigator.vibrate
candidates.evidence: 2026 casual UI couples visual payoff to haptics; our traffic is phone-first

candidates.name: A Connections-style grouping daily
candidates.evidence: The single most-played daily puzzle format in 2026, and a mechanic we have none of

candidates.name: A twist on a classic we already ship (e.g. Really Bad Chess's randomised armies)
candidates.evidence: Puzzmo's lineup leans on modernised classics; ours are classics with no twist at all

candidates.name: Show the puzzle before it starts
candidates.evidence: Puzzmo previews puzzles to let players plan; on a browse page it is also the whole pitch

candidates.name: A Wordle-style word daily, from a curated answer list
candidates.evidence: The largest single audience in the category — and the most cloned thing on the web
candidates.constraint: The obligation is the CURATION, not the mechanic. Wordle needs a hand-picked answer list because a random dictionary word makes an unfair puzzle. See word-generated for the version that owes nothing.

candidates.name: Real-time .io multiplayer
candidates.evidence: A durable top-ten category — and a persistent server, which our $100/month ceiling does not have
candidates.constraint: Rejected twice: the $100/month ceiling has no persistent server, and a multiplayer game with no audience is unplayable where a single-player one is merely unplayed.

candidates.name: Restyle the site in frosted glass
candidates.evidence: Named a 2026 gaming-UI trend — which is also the argument against dating the site to 2026
candidates.constraint: Rejected on taste, not cost: it dates the site to one year.

candidates.name: A generated word game — anagrams, from a word list
candidates.evidence: `word` is the largest gap in the survey at 2612 points across 21 posts, and we ship none of it. An anagram or word-ladder puzzle is generated from a static word list and verified solvable, exactly like our Sudoku — so it reaches that audience without owing a puzzle a day
candidates.constraint: Added after noticing the landscape had priced the whole `word` mechanic at 365 puzzles a year. That is the cost of CURATION, not of words: our Sudoku generates a fresh solvable puzzle daily from a seed and owes nothing.
